The failing spec is phase margin (65.75° vs. 70°). The only single-element change that moves it in the right direction by a meaningful amount is M4. Its +20% sensitivity of -4.79° is the largest in the table, and the sign fits an oversized mirror device. M4 hangs its gate capacitance on the mirror node `a`, which sets the non-dominant pole p2 ≈ gm3/C_a. A larger M4 lowers p2 toward UGBW and erodes phase margin. M3 is second because it is the diode-connected half of the same mirror and sets gm3 at that node. M1 is third because its drain capacitance loads node `a` with a smaller effect.

```json
{"ranking": ["M4", "M3", "M1"], "fault": "M4 (PMOS mirror output device) is oversized: W=7.506 um gives a mirror ratio of about 6.67 against M3 (W=1.126 um, same L). The extra gate capacitance at mirror node a lowers the non-dominant pole gm3/C_a toward UGBW, costing about 6 deg of phase margin. Restoring M4 to a smaller width consistent with the intended mirror ratio should bring PM back above 70 deg."}
```
